<p><strong>FURTHER INFORMATION</strong></p>
<ul>
<li><span data-olk-copy-source="MessageBody">Pagemasters Zine Fair is self funded by Pagemasters, with no external funding. Space and staff support are provided free of charge by South London Gallery.</span></li>
<li><span data-olk-copy-source="MessageBody">Pagemasters is a Risograph printing studio based in Lewisham, south London, specialising in zines, artist books, prints and workshops. Founded in 2017 by Justin Bailey and Jordan Taylor, the studio prints for independent publishers, artists and small presses, and runs Pagemasters Zine Fair each year to celebrate DIY and self published work. Alongside client printing, Pagemasters produces its own zines and runs workshops introducing people to Risograph printing and independent publishing</span></li>
<li>Content varies by stall holder and may include mature themes, so it suits visitors comfortable with a wide range of independent and DIY publishing content.</li>
</ul>

All weekend, 12 – 6pm, children and families are invited to have fun and be creative in the Orozco Garden. </span></p>
<p><span class="ui-provider gp b c d e f g h i j k l m n o p q r s t u v w x y z ab ac ae af ag ah ai aj ak" dir="ltr">Join us at the South London Gallery and find out more about the unique sculptural work, created by artist Gabriel Orozco. Created by the SLG’s Education team, this free worksheet offer prompts for young people of all ages to explore the plants and spaces outside.</span></p>
<p><span class="ui-provider gp b c d e f g h i j k l m n o p q r s t u v w x y z ab ac ae af ag ah ai aj ak" dir="ltr">The garden trail is available for free to explore the gardens at the South London Gallery every weekend. </span></p>
<p>Aimed at young people aged 5-12 years.</p>
<p><strong>ACCESS</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>The Orozco Garden has various levels and steps. The ground level is fully accessible.</li>
<li>There are accessible toilets.</li>
<li>Seating is available on request, please ask a Gallery Assistant if you would like a seat.</li>
<li><span data-contrast="auto">Please contact <a href="mailto:mail@southlondongallery.org">mail@southlondongallery.org</a> with access requirements and any questions.</span></li>

                <div class="x_elementToProof">Join artist <a href="https://www.tiharasmith.com/">Tihara Smith</a> for an exciting family workshop exploring textiles, colour and The Caribbean.</div>
<div class="x_elementToProof"></div>
<h3 class="x_elementToProof"><b>ABOUT FAMILY SPACE JUN – AUG 2026</b></h3>
<div class="x_elementToProof">
<p><span data-contrast="none">Family Space is a relaxed, creative workshop designed for families to explore and make together. Sessions are artist-led but you can join any time and take part at your own pace.</span><span data-ccp-props="{"134233117":false,"134233118":false,"335559738":240,"335559739":240}"> </span></p>
<ul>
<li data-leveltext="" data-font="Symbol" data-listid="1" data-list-defn-props="{"335552541":1,"335559685":720,"335559991":360,"469769226":"Symbol","469769242":[8226],"469777803":"left","469777804":"","469777815":"hybridMultilevel"}" data-aria-posinset="1" data-aria-level="1"><span data-contrast="none">Creative, fun sessions for children aged 5–12 years with parents/carers </span><span data-ccp-props="{"134233117":false,"134233118":false,"335559738":0,"335559739":0}"> </span></li>
<li data-leveltext="" data-font="Symbol" data-listid="1" data-list-defn-props="{"335552541":1,"335559685":720,"335559991":360,"469769226":"Symbol","469769242":[8226],"469777803":"left","469777804":"","469777815":"hybridMultilevel"}" data-aria-posinset="1" data-aria-level="1"><span data-contrast="none">Takes place on the last Saturday of each month, from 11am–1pm </span><span data-ccp-props="{"134233117":false,"134233118":false,"335559738":0,"335559739":0}"> </span></li>
<li data-leveltext="" data-font="Symbol" data-listid="1" data-list-defn-props="{"335552541":1,"335559685":720,"335559991":360,"469769226":"Symbol","469769242":[8226],"469777803":"left","469777804":"","469777815":"hybridMultilevel"}" data-aria-posinset="1" data-aria-level="1"><span data-contrast="none">Free, donations welcome</span><span data-ccp-props="{"134233117":false,"134233118":false,"335559738":0,"335559739":0}"> </span></li>
<li data-leveltext="" data-font="Symbol" data-listid="1" data-list-defn-props="{"335552541":1,"335559685":720,"335559991":360,"469769226":"Symbol","469769242":[8226],"469777803":"left","469777804":"","469777815":"hybridMultilevel"}" data-aria-posinset="1" data-aria-level="1"><span data-contrast="none">No booking required, drop in anytime. You can register online in advance to save time on the day, further information below.</span><span data-ccp-props="{"134233117":false,"134233118":false,"335559738":0,"335559739":0}"> </span></li>
<li data-leveltext="" data-font="Symbol" data-listid="1" data-list-defn-props="{"335552541":1,"335559685":720,"335559991":360,"469769226":"Symbol","469769242":[8226],"469777803":"left","469777804":"","469777815":"hybridMultilevel"}" data-aria-posinset="1" data-aria-level="1"><span data-contrast="none">First come, first served. There may be a short wait during busy periods. </span><span data-ccp-props="{"134233117":false,"134233118":false,"335559738":0,"335559739":0}"> </span></li>
</ul>
<p><span data-contrast="none">The space is supported by the SLG’s Communities and Learning team and is designed to be welcoming, inclusive and informal.</span></p>
</div>
<div class="x_elementToProof">From June to August 2026, sessions will be led by Family Space Artist in Residence, Tihara Smith <a id="OWA0bd2f52f-e7aa-5460-18bf-0cf36b2e6eb7" class="x_OWAAutoLink" title="https://www.johnmacedo.co.uk/" href="https://www.johnmacedo.co.uk/" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" data-linkindex="0" data-auth="NotApplicable"></a>. The residency will end in August with a moment to celebrate the collective work of participating families.</div>
<h3 class="x_elementToProof"><b>ABOUT TIHARA SMITH</b></h3>
<div class="x_elementToProof">
<p><span data-contrast="auto">Tihara Smith is a fashion designer and textile artist inspired by Caribbean culture and the Windrush Generation. Known for her raffia embroidery, she celebrates her heritage through vibrant design, workshops, and collaborations. Her work has been acquired by the London Museum and she has worked with institutions like the V&A and Somerset House. Tihara was selected as one of The King’s Foundation’s 35 Under 35, and in 2026 published her first book Raffia Embroidery: Vibrant Designs Inspired by the Caribbean.</span><span data-ccp-props="{"201341983":0,"335559739":0,"335559740":240}"> </span></p>
<p><span data-contrast="auto">Tihara also creates Caribbean-inspired stationery, accessories, and greeting cards.</span><span data-ccp-props="{}"> </span></p>
</div>
<h3><strong>ACCESS</strong></h3>
<p><span data-contrast="none">The room is likely to be noisy.</span><span data-ccp-props="{"134233117":false,"134233118":false,"335559738":0,"335559739":0}"><br />
</span><span data-contrast="auto">Sensory materials are available on request.</span><span data-ccp-props="{"134233117":false,"134233118":false,"335559738":240,"335559739":240}"><br />
</span><span data-contrast="auto">This event is seated.</span><span data-ccp-props="{"134233117":false,"134233118":false,"335559738":240,"335559739":240}"><br />
</span><span data-contrast="auto">Ear plugs, ear defenders, magnifying glasses and wheelchairs are all available.</span><span data-ccp-props="{}"> </span></p>
<p><span data-olk-copy-source="MessageBody">Please note that Family Space runs on a first come first serve basis and you may be required to wait a short while for a space to become available if we are at maximum capacity</span></p>
<h3><strong>REGISTRATION</strong></h3>
<p><span data-contrast="none">To save time on the day, you can register online in advance.</span></p>
<p><span data-contrast="none">Please note: each attendee (adults and children) must be registered individually.</span><span data-ccp-props="{"134233117":false,"134233118":false,"335559738":240,"335559739":240}"> </span></p>
<h3>SUPPORT US</h3>
<p>Support the SLG’s programme for children, families and young people by <a href="https://shop.southlondongallery.org/products/donation" target="_blank" rel="noopener">donating today</a>. Every donation helps us to keep the gallery and its activities free, and realise our ambition for contemporary art to be accessible to all.</p>

				const lazyloadRunObserver = () => {
					const lazyloadBackgrounds = document.querySelectorAll( `.e-con.e-parent:not(.e-lazyloaded)` );
					const lazyloadBackgroundObserver = new IntersectionObserver( ( entries ) => {
						entries.forEach( ( entry ) => {
							if ( entry.isIntersecting ) {
								let lazyloadBackground = entry.target;
								if( lazyloadBackground ) {
									lazyloadBackground.classList.add( 'e-lazyloaded' );
								}
								lazyloadBackgroundObserver.unobserve( entry.target );
							}
						});
					}, { rootMargin: '200px 0px 200px 0px' } );
					lazyloadBackgrounds.forEach( ( lazyloadBackground ) => {
						lazyloadBackgroundObserver.observe( lazyloadBackground );
					} );
				};
				const events = [
					'DOMContentLoaded',
					'elementor/lazyload/observe',
				];
				events.forEach( ( event ) => {
					document.addEventListener( event, lazyloadRunObserver );
				} );
			</script>

				const lazyloadRunObserver = () => {
					const lazyloadBackgrounds = document.querySelectorAll( `.e-con.e-parent:not(.e-lazyloaded)` );
					const lazyloadBackgroundObserver = new IntersectionObserver( ( entries ) => {
						entries.forEach( ( entry ) => {
							if ( entry.isIntersecting ) {
								let lazyloadBackground = entry.target;
								if( lazyloadBackground ) {
									lazyloadBackground.classList.add( 'e-lazyloaded' );
								}
								lazyloadBackgroundObserver.unobserve( entry.target );
							}
						});
					}, { rootMargin: '200px 0px 200px 0px' } );
					lazyloadBackgrounds.forEach( ( lazyloadBackground ) => {
						lazyloadBackgroundObserver.observe( lazyloadBackground );
					} );
				};
				const events = [
					'DOMContentLoaded',
					'elementor/lazyload/observe',
				];
				events.forEach( ( event ) => {
					document.addEventListener( event, lazyloadRunObserver );
				} );
			</script>

				const lazyloadRunObserver = () => {
					const lazyloadBackgrounds = document.querySelectorAll( `.e-con.e-parent:not(.e-lazyloaded)` );
					const lazyloadBackgroundObserver = new IntersectionObserver( ( entries ) => {
						entries.forEach( ( entry ) => {
							if ( entry.isIntersecting ) {
								let lazyloadBackground = entry.target;
								if( lazyloadBackground ) {
									lazyloadBackground.classList.add( 'e-lazyloaded' );
								}
								lazyloadBackgroundObserver.unobserve( entry.target );
							}
						});
					}, { rootMargin: '200px 0px 200px 0px' } );
					lazyloadBackgrounds.forEach( ( lazyloadBackground ) => {
						lazyloadBackgroundObserver.observe( lazyloadBackground );
					} );
				};
				const events = [
					'DOMContentLoaded',
					'elementor/lazyload/observe',
				];
				events.forEach( ( event ) => {
					document.addEventListener( event, lazyloadRunObserver );
				} );
			</script>

              <p>🟥DANCE FOR SHAKA🟥</p>
<p>👑 Celebrating The Legendary King Of Sound System Jah Shaka 👑</p>
<p>🔊 Night Warehouse Session 🔈</p>
<p>🌴AUGUST CARNIVAL WEEKEND🌴</p>
<p>SUNDAY 30 AUGUST 2026</p>
<p>10pm-5am @ EGG LDN, Kigs Cross, London N7 9AP</p>
<p>Commemorating & celebrating the KING Of Sound System, The Mighty Zulu Warrior Jah Shaka!</p>
<p>JAH SHAKA SOUND SYSTEM</p>
<p>Meets YOUNG WARRIOR SOUND SYSTEM</p>
<p>Switching on & Stringing up together on the dance-floor in the main arena❗️</p>
<p>After a mesmerising Sold Out 2025 Young Warrior brings you another musical & HISTORIC event switching on and linking the Legendary Jah Shaka Sound System alongside his own sound system in the massive Archive’s (Club 360) warehouse main arena!</p>
<p>Digging through one of the most prolific musical vaults in time this is a dance NOT TO BE MISSED as the Shaka legacy continues!</p>
<p>Young Warrior – “It is an honour and an emotional moment in time to be able to do something like this for my father, carry on the torch & be a generational bridge for this and the next generation to experience what is like the Pyramids of Dub!</p>
<p>Shaka always say “Let Jah Music play” and so it shall be!</p>
<p>2025 we did this for the first time now due to popular public demand we take over an even bigger arena where we can bring out even more boxes!”</p>
<p>⚡️Fresh Shaka Merchandise, Unheard & Original Shaka Archive Dubplates, Shaka Vinyl Selection, Decoration Installations, Outdoor Garden & smoking area, Full vibes, Bar & More!</p>
<p>📍@ EGG LDN, 5-13 VALE ROYAL, KINGS CROSS, LONDON, N7 9AP</p>
<p>🚂 Train: Kings cross / Caledonian Road</p>
<p>🚎 24 Hour Bus Service & Night Tube</p>
<p>🚘 FREE Sunday Parking Available On Surrounding Roads</p>
<p>🎟️ Tickets 🎟️</p>

<p>▪️£26 +b/f Second Release in advance online (*Enter At Anytime before 2AM*)</p>
<p>▪️More on the door</p>
<p>🟥STRICT 2AM LAST ENTRY – I.D REQUIRED FOR ENTRY🟥</p>

				const lazyloadRunObserver = () => {
					const lazyloadBackgrounds = document.querySelectorAll( `.e-con.e-parent:not(.e-lazyloaded)` );
					const lazyloadBackgroundObserver = new IntersectionObserver( ( entries ) => {
						entries.forEach( ( entry ) => {
							if ( entry.isIntersecting ) {
								let lazyloadBackground = entry.target;
								if( lazyloadBackground ) {
									lazyloadBackground.classList.add( 'e-lazyloaded' );
								}
								lazyloadBackgroundObserver.unobserve( entry.target );
							}
						});
					}, { rootMargin: '200px 0px 200px 0px' } );
					lazyloadBackgrounds.forEach( ( lazyloadBackground ) => {
						lazyloadBackgroundObserver.observe( lazyloadBackground );
					} );
				};
				const events = [
					'DOMContentLoaded',
					'elementor/lazyload/observe',
				];
				events.forEach( ( event ) => {
					document.addEventListener( event, lazyloadRunObserver );
				} );
			</script>

          <h1 class="main-title">Egg LDN Pres: Carnival Special Closing Party</h1>
          <div class="booking-details">
                        <p class="date">SUNDAY 30TH AUGUST 2026</p>
                        <p class="time">23:00 - 05:00</p>
                      </div>
          <div class="book-button-groups">
            <a target="_blank" href="https://www.tixr.com/groups/egglondon/events/egg-ldn-pres-carnival-special-closing-party-198741" class="buy-button">BUY TICKETS</a>
            <a href="https://tixr.com/e/198741"  target="_blank" class="book-button">BOOK A TABLE <span><img src="/wp-content/themes/playful-child/images/arrow-right.png" alt=""></span> </a>          </div>
          <div class="condition-details">
              <p>The annual carnival weekender is back and ready to roll on Sunday 30th August! Get set for a feel-good mix of <strong>House, Funky House & Soulful House</strong>, bringing uplifting grooves, soulful vocals and plenty of energy to the dancefloor.</p>
<p><strong>Entry Policy at Egg London</strong></p>
<p>Egg London is a strictly 18+ venue. To enhance safety and security, we have installed a Club Scan system at the front door. All guests are required to present a valid physical form of photo ID for scanning upon entry. Acceptable forms of ID include an unexpired passport, driving license, provisional driving license, or a photo card featuring the PASS hologram. Please note that photocopies, digital images, or screenshots of IDs will not be accepted under any circumstances.</p>
<p>Thank you for your cooperation in ensuring a safe and smooth entry process.</p>

					const lazyloadBackgrounds = document.querySelectorAll( `.e-con.e-parent:not(.e-lazyloaded)` );
					const lazyloadBackgroundObserver = new IntersectionObserver( ( entries ) => {
						entries.forEach( ( entry ) => {
							if ( entry.isIntersecting ) {
								let lazyloadBackground = entry.target;
								if( lazyloadBackground ) {
									lazyloadBackground.classList.add( 'e-lazyloaded' );
								}
								lazyloadBackgroundObserver.unobserve( entry.target );
							}
						});
					}, { rootMargin: '200px 0px 200px 0px' } );
					lazyloadBackgrounds.forEach( ( lazyloadBackground ) => {
						lazyloadBackgroundObserver.observe( lazyloadBackground );
					} );
				};
				const events = [
					'DOMContentLoaded',
					'elementor/lazyload/observe',
				];
				events.forEach( ( event ) => {
					document.addEventListener( event, lazyloadRunObserver );
				} );
			</script>

          <div class="book-button-groups">

          <div class="condition-details">
              <p>Every Wednesday, Wednesday Club brings house, tech house, electro and hip hop to Egg London — made for students and anyone looking to switch off before the weekend.</p>
<p><strong>📍 Egg London</strong><br /><strong>🕥 22:30 – 04:00</strong><br /><strong>🎟 Free entry before 00:00 + free shot (online claim required)</strong><br /><strong>🎵 House · Tech House · Electro · Hip Hop</strong><br /><strong>🍸 £5 selected drinks all night</strong></p>
<p><strong>Entry Policy at Egg London</strong></p>
<p>Egg London is a strictly 18+ venue. To enhance safety and security, we have installed a Club Scan system at the front door. All guests are required to present a valid physical form of photo ID for scanning upon entry. Acceptable forms of ID include an unexpired passport, driving license, provisional driving license, or a photo card featuring the PASS hologram. Please note that photocopies, digital images, or screenshots of IDs will not be accepted under any circumstances.</p>
<p>Thank you for your cooperation in ensuring a safe and smooth entry process.</p>

					} );
				};

					'elementor/lazyload/observe',

				} );

600 Years On Strings

Delivered with Applied Live Art Studio (ALAS) CIC

We’re excited to celebrate our 65th birthday with an ambitious heritage project, funded by The National Lottery Heritage Fund, to revive and preserve the future of marionette puppetry in the UK, an endangered craft with more than 600 years of history.

This summer we will be producing a landmark public programme to celebrate this momentous occasion: including a new marionette performance on the restored historic marionette bridges, a panel talk, exhibition, masterclasses and a published guide! See below for a full outline of the events.

“This feels like the culmination of over five years of dedication and advocacy for the much loved yet endangered craft of marionette making. Thanks to the support of many organisations who have invested in myself and Little Angel Theatre, including Queen Elizabeth Scholarship Trust (QEST), Heritage Crafts, and now The National Lottery Heritage Fund, we can finally work towards bringing this artform to life on stage as well as safeguarding it for the next generation of makers and audiences alike.”
Oliver Hyman, Associate Director

MARIONETTE: A DIY Guide to Making Your Own 9-String Puppet

To mark our 65th anniversary, Little Angel Theatre is publishing a book that’s a step-by-step guide to building your own 9-string marionette using nothing but basic hand tools. But its much more than that! It’s also a catalogue of some of the artists who’ve kept this craft alive across six decades, and essays about the craft and history. Contributions from Oliver Hymans, Sarah Wright and Stephen Mottram, alongside profiles of leading British marionette makers past and present.

£9.99 | Published by Social Art Publications | Launches 21 August 2026

When everyone has left the house in the morning, the bath toys spring into action and head off on exciting adventures in their magical flying bath! How does it work?

Tickets cost £7 per household. There is an optional donation fee to help those who face barriers, access our work.

You will receive an automatic email confirming your purchase, and a further email containing the Vimeo link and password will be sent at the start of the access time stated next to your chosen show, above.

The password will give you access to the film from the times stated below (please note that times vary depending on which show you have booked). You can watch the film as many times as you like during this period, but you will not be able to access it after the stated expiration times.

Please note, you can buy the film after the start time but access will still expire at the stated time. If you buy it during box office hours (found here), you will receive the link and password within an hour, but if outside those times, our box office will be in touch during opening hours.

Ps. This offer is an addition to our in-house performances, not a replacement. 

Visit Vimeo’s help centre for technical and streaming queries, here.

If you have any queries in regards to your booking, please contact our Box Office: [email protected] 

Please consider donating to help those who might face barriers access our work

Our digital work enables us to reach those who might face access barriers to visiting our venues. These could be geographical, physical or socio-economic.

If you are able to make a donation to help us subsidise this area of work we would be grateful – the income from the ticket sales alone does not cover our costs to create these digital assets.

At the point of checkout, an optional donation charge of £7.00 will be suggested for your order for you to “pass it forward” to a family to access this performance – this could be a subscriber to our Puppets For All scheme, a child who is in hospital or long term care and their family, or a beneficiary from a local community partner organisation (for example Islington Centre for Refugees and Migrants).

To celebrate our 65th birthday, we’re bringing together historic and newly made marionettes in a landmark exhibition.  For the first time in a generation, we will be showcasing work by leading British makers across six decades, from Little Angel Theatre founders John and Lyndie Wright to a new generation of artists.

Through this collection of puppets and objects, we hope to reconnect the theatre’s present with the original collections that helped shape its history, taking advantage of a rare opportunity to showcase a historic marionette collection in direct dialogue with our brand new marionette production, The Sorcerer’s Apprentice.

Fewer than five people in Britain currently make a living carving marionettes. This is the story of how that happened — and what we’re doing about it.

The exhibition is free but you need to book a timeslot to visit. More information about coming to the exhibition can be found further down this page.

The Story

In 1662, Samuel Pepys watched a marionette Punch and Judy show in Covent Garden and wrote about it in his diary. It’s one of the earliest records of a British tradition that runs, unbroken, through fairground booths and Victorian theatres to Muffin the Mule and Gerry Anderson’s Supermarionation  all the way to a converted temperance hall in Islington, where John Wright founded Little Angel Theatre in 1961 and gave marionette puppetry a permanent home in the UK for the first time.

Today, that thread is close to breaking. Marionette-making is listed on the Heritage Crafts Red List of Endangered Crafts. Unlike most puppetry disciplines, it has no college course, no apprenticeship scheme, no formal route in at all — only the slow, hands-on transmission of knowledge from one maker to the next. Little Angel Theatre is one of only a handful of theatres in the world still equipped with a marionette bridge, the elevated rig marionette performers work from, and we’re using our 65th anniversary with support from The National Lottery Heritage Fund to restore it, train new makers and puppeteers, and stage a brand-new production.

This exhibition is where the past and future meet. This is a celebration of marionettes from across six decades of British puppetry, shown alongside the live workshop, rehearsal room and stage where the craft is being kept alive right now.

“Endangered crafts survive because people choose to practise them, teach them and pass them on. If this exhibition helps even a handful of people discover the same fascination I felt standing backstage at the Little Angel Theatre all those years ago, looking up at those silent figures hanging patiently above me, then perhaps we have helped ensure that marionettes will continue to dance for generations yet to come.”
— Oliver Hymans, Associate Director, Little Angel Theatre

 

Featuring puppets made by John and Lyndie Wright, Stephen Mottram, Jan Zalud, Ash Appadu, Maria Herbert-Liew., Gren Middleton, John Kaye, Sarah Vigars, Oliver Hymans and Peter O’Rourke as well as puppets lent by Miranda Lewis-Brown, Jose Navarro and Stan Middleton.

Visitor Information

This free exhibition takes place in Little Angel Theatre’s Puppet Workshop at 41 Cross Street, N1 2BB, just short walk from our Theatre.

Booking times are a flexible window of arrival within the hour to manage visitor numbers.

The exhibition takes place across two floors. Unfortunately, there is no step free access to the basement section of this exhibition, however, we will be recording the downstairs installation and can provide digital access upon request. If you have any questions about accessing this event please contact [email protected].

All ages are welcome at the exhibition but please bear in mind that it has not been specially designed for very young children. The exhibits are not interactive and visitors are asked not to touch them.

Please note that you will be required to park any buggies or large luggage outside in our walkway area. We cannot be held responsible for loss or damage of property left outside the exhibition.

A curious child unleashes magical powers, with the ability to transform everyday objects into the extraordinary! But when the spells don’t stop, the young apprentice learns that all things must be handled with care, especially magic.

This spellbinding show, inspired by Goethe’s classic poem, celebrates and restores the endangered art of marionette puppetry at Little Angel Theatre.

Don’t miss this magical highlight of the Children’s Puppet Festival, featuring handcrafted puppets from Little Angel Theatre’s workshops.

This show is proudly supported by the National Heritage Lottery Fund.

Age Guidance

The Sorcerer’s Apprentice is aimed at ages 6-11. Our shows for this age group have storylines that can be followed by children from around age 6. They work for a wide age range and there will be elements to engage the older children, and adults, in the audience, for example music, puppetry techniques, more complex ideas, language or humour. Children under the recommended age can often enjoy the visuals but may not follow everything, and may not stay engaged. If the show contains any parts likely to be scary or upsetting for anyone, these will be mentioned in the FAQ below.

How will we be seated?

This show has standard theatre seating – rows of benches facing the stage. There will be up to 90 people watching the show.

Can children join in?

This isn’t an interactive show and there are no parts where the audience are asked to contribute. The audience stay in their seats while watching, but you can leave and re-enter the auditorium at any time.

Is there anything that might be scary?

The story explores themes like responsibility, curiosity, and consequences of misusing power. There are a few mildly tense scenes, such as when the magic gets out of control and objects start moving on their own. These moments are designed to be exciting rather than frightening, and they resolve quickly. There may be comic chaos (like objects flying around or exaggerated magical mishaps), but nothing intended to be harmful or realistic.

You think know the story of the Pied Piper of Hamelin ?— But do you? 

Here’s the tale of Horatio, the brave little rat behind the legend. When Horatio escapes the dull life of an ordinary river rat for the sights, sounds and smells of Hamelin, he soon finds himself caught up in a whirlwind of adventure. 

His imprisonment sparks a rat invasion, the arrival of the mysterious Pied Piper, and a heroic tale waiting to be told. With puppetry, storytelling and original music, The Pied Piper: A Rat’s Tale is a funny and imaginative family show that reveals the story behind the story.

Age Guidance

The Pied Piper: A Rat’s Tale is for everyone over 5. Our shows for this age group have storylines that can be followed by children from around age 5. They work for a wide age range and there will be elements for the older children and adults in the audience to appreciate, for example music, puppetry techniques, more complex ideas, language or humour. Children under the recommended age can often enjoy the visuals but may not follow everything, and may not stay engaged. If the show contains any parts likely to be scary or upsetting for anyone, these will be mentioned in the FAQ below.

Please note that this is a new production which premiere in September. It is still in development and the details in the guidance FAQs may be updated as we know more about the specifics of the show.

How will we be seated?

This show has standard seating for our studios. There are rows with chairs and soft blocks facing the stage, and mats on the floor at the front. There will be up to 65 people watching the show (sometimes more if you come when there are school groups).

Can children join in?

There will be verbal interaction with the performer. The audience stay in their seats while watching, but you can leave and re-enter the auditorium at any time.

Is there anything that might be scary?

There is some mild threat from the mysterious figure of the piper.

What can I use to prepare my child or help to decide if the show is right for them?

A visual story will be available soon after the show opens.

Pip and Posy Live on Stage

19 Sep–22 Nov 2026

Aimed at ages 2-5

Duration: 50 minutes approx

Book Tickets
£16.00 Adult £14.00 Child (age 1-17)

 

All tickets are £8 at previews Sat 19 – Sun 20 September
All tickets are £8.50 at 4.45pm shows on Wednesdays
All tickets are £10 at 4.5pm shows on Fridays

If the performance you’re interested in is sold out, you can join our waiting list here.

At Little Angel Theatre

14 Dagmar Passage, London N1 2DN

Plan your visit

From the producers of The Smartest Giant in Town comes a brand-new theatre show bursting with friendship and fun, Pip and Posy Live on Stage.

Inspired by the BAFTA nominated animated series from Magic Light Pictures and based on the picture books by multi-award-winning illustrator Axel Scheffler (The Gruffalo) this exciting new live stage show celebrates the power of imagination, kindness, and creativity for little ones and families everywhere.

Pip and Posy are best friends whose lives revolve around the world of play. Their stories are a joyful celebration of friendship in all its forms – the laughter, the ups and downs, the silliness, and care. Together with their friends Mo and Jamila, they head off on a thrilling adventure through tangled jungles, across slimy swamps, and high above the clouds aboard a big red balloon. Just watch out, the Troll is after the treasure!

Packed with toe-tapping songs, stunning puppets, and irresistible interactive play, Pip and Posy are waiting for you. Come on, let’s play!

Age Guidance

Pip and Posy Live on Stage is aimed at ages 2-5. Our shows for this age group are lively but gentle, with simple stories and appealing characters. Small children are kept engaged with visual wonders and effective use of music and language.

Please note that this is a new production which premieres in September. It is still in development, and the details in the age guidance FAQ may be updated as we know more about the specifics of the show.

How will we be seated?

This show has standard theatre seating – rows of benches facing the stage. There will be up to 90 people watching the show (sometimes more if you come when there are school groups).

Can children join in?

We welcome vocal responses, and there may be parts in the show where you are invited to join in with words or actions. the audience stay in their seats while watching, but you can leave and re-enter the auditorium at any time.

Is there anything that might be scary?

There is nothing very likely to be scary. Posy is scared at first when Pip pretends to be a troll, but is fine when she realises it’s her friend dressing up. They also pretend they are travelling across a swamp of crocodiles, but this is all imaginative play.

Should I bring a child under two?

All ages are welcome at our shows and age ranges can only be a rough guide, but please bear in mind that Pip and Posy Live on Stage was not specially designed for babies and toddlers. A show recommended from under age two would usually have more relaxed seating, smaller audience numbers and strong sensory and interactive elements.

What can I use to prepare my child or help to decide if the show is right for them?

The show is inspired by the animated series from Magic Light Pictures and based on the picture books by Axel Scheffler. You can watch the series here

<div class="wp-block-cover alignfull" style="min-height:681px;aspect-ratio:unset;" data-block-type="core"><img fetchpriority="high" decoding="async" width="5760" height="3840" class="wp-block-cover__image-background wp-image-35554 size-full" alt="" src="https://www.wacarts.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Schools-Festival-image-resized-1.jpg" data-object-fit="cover"/><span aria-hidden="true" class="wp-block-cover__background has-background-dim" style="background-color:#441d1d"></span><div class="wp-block-cover__inner-container is-layout-constrained wp-block-cover-is-layout-constrained">
<div class="wp-block-stackable-heading stk-block-heading stk-block-heading--v2 stk-block stk-b901ba3" id="span-style-color-var-nv-site-bg-class-stk-highlight-schools-festival-programme-2024-25-span" data-block-id="b901ba3"><h2 class="stk-block-heading__text has-text-align-center"><span style="color: var(--nv-site-bg);" class="stk-highlight">Schools Festival 2027 </span></h2></div>
</div></div>



<div class="wp-block-stackable-divider stk-block-divider has-text-align-center stk-block stk-yotf7ht" data-block-id="yotf7ht"><hr class="stk-block-divider__hr"/></div>



<p class="has-text-align-center has-medium-font-size wp-block-paragraph">Following the success of the 25/26 Festival we are thrilled to launch Wac Arts Schools Festival 2027. The Wac Arts School Festival is a programme of workshops facilitated by industry professionals culminating with all participating schools coming together at Wac Arts in the Old Town Hall on the <strong>27<sup>th</sup> May 2027</strong> to celebrate and share their work.</p>



<p class="has-text-align-center has-medium-font-size wp-block-paragraph">We are excited to offer the opportunity for secondary school students to devise and create original performances, films/animations and/or curate an exhibition inspired by this year’s theme: <span style="color: var(--nv-dark-bg);" class="stk-highlight"><strong>The World Within, The World Around.</strong></span></p>



<div class="wp-block-ugb-container ugb-container ugb-81059d9 ugb-container--v2 ugb-container--design-basic ugb-main-block"><div class="ugb-inner-block"><div class="ugb-block-content"><div class="ugb-container__wrapper ugb-81059d9-wrapper"><div class="ugb-container__side"><div class="ugb-container__content-wrapper ugb-81059d9-content-wrapper">
<p class="has-text-align-center wp-block-paragraph"><span style="color: var(--nv-dark-bg);" class="stk-highlight"><strong>Schools can submit Creative Project Groups formed of 10-25 young people (Year 7-10) to devise:</strong></span></p>



<h4 class="wp-block-heading has-text-align-center" data-block-type="core"><span style="color: var(--nv-c-1);" class="stk-highlight">A Live Performance</span></h4>



<p class="has-text-align-center wp-block-paragraph">Dance, Music, Physical Theatre, Spoken Word, Theatre etc.</p>



<p class="has-text-align-center wp-block-paragraph"><strong>And/Or</strong></p>



<h4 class="wp-block-heading has-text-align-center" data-block-type="core"><span style="color: var(--nv-c-1);" class="stk-highlight">A Creative Arts Exhibition</span></h4>



<p class="has-text-align-center wp-block-paragraph">Animation, Collage, Textiles, Photography, Painting, Visual Arts etc.</p>
</div></div></div></div></div></div>



<div class="wp-block-ugb-container ugb-container ugb-be185ef ugb-container--v2 ugb-container--design-basic ugb-main-block"><div class="ugb-inner-block"><div class="ugb-block-content"><div class="ugb-container__wrapper ugb-be185ef-wrapper"><div class="ugb-container__side"><div class="ugb-container__content-wrapper ugb-be185ef-content-wrapper">
<h4 class="wp-block-heading has-text-align-center" data-block-type="core"><span style="color: var(--nv-c-1);" class="stk-highlight">Participating schools will receive</span></h4>



<p class="has-text-align-center wp-block-paragraph">· Up to 10 hours of creative workshops with professional artists. .</p>



<p class="has-text-align-center wp-block-paragraph">· Personalised workshops for your timetable and students.</p>



<p class="has-text-align-center wp-block-paragraph">· A festival day celebrating students work in the form of a performance or exhibition on Thursday 27<sup>th</sup> May 2027.</p>
</div></div></div></div></div></div>



<div class="wp-block-ugb-container ugb-container ugb-5d5b00b ugb-container--v2 ugb-container--design-basic ugb-main-block"><div class="ugb-inner-block"><div class="ugb-block-content"><div class="ugb-container__wrapper ugb-5d5b00b-wrapper"><div class="ugb-container__side"><div class="ugb-container__content-wrapper ugb-5d5b00b-content-wrapper">
<h4 class="wp-block-heading has-text-align-center" data-block-type="core"><span style="color: var(--nv-c-1);" class="stk-highlight">Cost</span></h4>



<p class="has-text-align-center wp-block-paragraph"><strong>The fee per Creative Project Group for the 2027 Schools Festival Programme is £600.</strong> Wac Arts heavily subsidise participating schools involved in the Schools Festival Programme, the full value equating to £2,600 per Creative Project Group.</p>



<div class="wp-block-stackable-spacer stk-block-spacer stk--no-padding stk-block stk-h53lnt2" data-block-id="h53lnt2"></div>



<h4 class="wp-block-heading has-text-align-center" data-block-type="core"><span style="color: var(--nv-c-1);" class="stk-highlight">Find OUT MORE</span></h4>



<p class="has-text-align-center wp-block-paragraph"><em>If you would like to discuss this project please email </em><strong><em>schools@wacarts.co.uk</em></strong><em> or to speak to a member of the team, please call Harriet on </em></p>



<p class="has-text-align-center wp-block-paragraph"><strong><em>020 7692 5800.</em></strong></p>

<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Fundraise For Wac Arts</strong></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Have you ever been inspired to run a marathon, swim the serpentine or even dance continuously for 24 hours? We regularly have entries in <strong>Challenge Events</strong>, such as the London Landmarks Half Marathon, The Big Half, Vitality 10k and Swim Serpentine. </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Would you like to go on an adventure, push your limits, achieve a lifetime goal – all whilst supporting Wac Arts?</strong> </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">We are currently recruiting for participants in the following events, click below to find out more.</p>



<ul class="wp-block-list" data-block-type="core">
<li data-block-type="core"><a href="https://forms.office.com/Pages/ResponsePage.aspx?id=r4FA6Lg2EkiPRe0PmHr95B2L5IT8TcxIkJSxlvSB3tVUMFo0TVdMUlE1SjJMOVhNMEhWTUNNNDVKTy4u">London Landmarks Half Marathon, Sunday 12th April 2026</a></li>
</ul>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">We are continually looking for more ways to get people involved so if you have any suggestions please do let us know.</p>

			<h1 class="entry-title">Book Tickets</h1>					</header><!-- .entry-header -->

		<div class="entry-content">
			
<p class="has-dark-gray-color has-text-color has-link-color wp-elements-1 wp-block-paragraph" style="font-size:16px"><strong>Evening performances normally start at 7.30 p.m. Matinees start at 3.00 p.m.</strong>  </p>



<p class="has-dark-gray-color has-text-color has-background has-link-color wp-elements-2 wp-block-paragraph" style="background-color:#ecebeb;font-size:15px"><br>Tickets for shows go on sale one month before each production’s opening performance.</p>



<p class="has-dark-gray-color has-text-color has-background has-link-color wp-elements-3 wp-block-paragraph" style="background-color:#ecebeb;font-size:15px">Members ticket price: <strong>£10</strong></p>



<p class="has-dark-gray-color has-text-color has-background has-link-color wp-elements-4 wp-block-paragraph" style="background-color:#ecebeb;font-size:15px">Non-Members ticket price:<strong> £13</strong></p>



<p class="has-dark-gray-color has-text-color has-background has-link-color wp-elements-5 wp-block-paragraph" style="background-color:#ecebeb;font-size:15px"><strong>Book tickets at</strong> <strong><a href="https://www.ticketsource.co.uk/theatre62" rel="nofollow">https://www.ticketsource.co.uk/theatre62</a></strong></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"></p>



<p class="has-dark-gray-color has-text-color has-link-color wp-elements-6 wp-block-paragraph" style="font-size:15px">Members and Non-Members can book online. There is no separate booking fee, which is included in the ticket price.</p>



<p class="has-dark-gray-color has-text-color has-link-color wp-elements-7 wp-block-paragraph" style="font-size:15px">Each online booking can be for any number of Non-Members and (optionally) one Member (i.e. only one Member ticket can be selected for each booking).</p>



<p class="has-dark-gray-color has-text-color has-link-color wp-elements-8 wp-block-paragraph" style="font-size:15px">If you are unable to book online, reservations can be made via:</p>



<ul class="wp-block-list">
<li class="has-dark-gray-color has-text-color has-link-color wp-elements-9" style="font-size:15px">email: boxoffice@theatre62.org.uk</li>
</ul>



<ul class="wp-block-list">
<li class="has-dark-gray-color has-text-color has-link-color wp-elements-10" style="font-size:15px">phone: 07542 716 888</li>
</ul>



<p class="has-dark-gray-color has-text-color has-link-color wp-elements-11 wp-block-paragraph" style="font-size:15px">When booking by email or phone, online bank transfer is also possible. Details are available from the box office.</p>



<p class="has-dark-gray-color has-text-color has-link-color wp-elements-12 wp-block-paragraph" style="font-size:15px">Please note <strong>the box office at the theatre is cashless</strong>, so payments on the door for reserved tickets should be made by card only.  Cash payments can be accepted, but only for the correct amount. Change cannot be given. Cheques made payable to  ‘Wickham Theatre Trust’ are also accepted.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph" style="font-size:15px"></p>

			<h1 class="entry-title">Book Tickets</h1>					</header><!-- .entry-header -->

		<div class="entry-content">
			
<p class="has-dark-gray-color has-text-color has-link-color wp-elements-1 wp-block-paragraph" style="font-size:16px"><strong>Evening performances normally start at 7.30 p.m. Matinees start at 3.00 p.m.</strong>  </p>



<p class="has-dark-gray-color has-text-color has-background has-link-color wp-elements-2 wp-block-paragraph" style="background-color:#ecebeb;font-size:15px"><br>Tickets for shows go on sale one month before each production’s opening performance.</p>



<p class="has-dark-gray-color has-text-color has-background has-link-color wp-elements-3 wp-block-paragraph" style="background-color:#ecebeb;font-size:15px">Members ticket price: <strong>£10</strong></p>



<p class="has-dark-gray-color has-text-color has-background has-link-color wp-elements-4 wp-block-paragraph" style="background-color:#ecebeb;font-size:15px">Non-Members ticket price:<strong> £13</strong></p>



<p class="has-dark-gray-color has-text-color has-background has-link-color wp-elements-5 wp-block-paragraph" style="background-color:#ecebeb;font-size:15px"><strong>Book tickets at</strong> <strong><a href="https://www.ticketsource.co.uk/theatre62" rel="nofollow">https://www.ticketsource.co.uk/theatre62</a></strong></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"></p>



<p class="has-dark-gray-color has-text-color has-link-color wp-elements-6 wp-block-paragraph" style="font-size:15px">Members and Non-Members can book online. There is no separate booking fee, which is included in the ticket price.</p>



<p class="has-dark-gray-color has-text-color has-link-color wp-elements-7 wp-block-paragraph" style="font-size:15px">Each online booking can be for any number of Non-Members and (optionally) one Member (i.e. only one Member ticket can be selected for each booking).</p>



<p class="has-dark-gray-color has-text-color has-link-color wp-elements-8 wp-block-paragraph" style="font-size:15px">If you are unable to book online, reservations can be made via:</p>



<ul class="wp-block-list">
<li class="has-dark-gray-color has-text-color has-link-color wp-elements-9" style="font-size:15px">email: boxoffice@theatre62.org.uk</li>
</ul>



<ul class="wp-block-list">
<li class="has-dark-gray-color has-text-color has-link-color wp-elements-10" style="font-size:15px">phone: 07542 716 888</li>
</ul>



<p class="has-dark-gray-color has-text-color has-link-color wp-elements-11 wp-block-paragraph" style="font-size:15px">When booking by email or phone, online bank transfer is also possible. Details are available from the box office.</p>



<p class="has-dark-gray-color has-text-color has-link-color wp-elements-12 wp-block-paragraph" style="font-size:15px">Please note <strong>the box office at the theatre is cashless</strong>, so payments on the door for reserved tickets should be made by card only.  Cash payments can be accepted, but only for the correct amount. Change cannot be given. Cheques made payable to  ‘Wickham Theatre Trust’ are also accepted.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph" style="font-size:15px"></p>

                    <div class="main-content__intro">
                <p>What happens when man’s best friend becomes head-of-state?</p>

            </div>
        
                    <div class="main-content__text  stack stack--l">
                <p><a href="https://halle.co.uk/">The Hallé</a> and <a href="https://opera-rara.com/">Opera Rara</a> join forces with the <a href="https://www.eno.org/about/chorus/">Chorus of English National Opera</a> to present <a href="https://www.eno.org/people/jacques-offenbach/">Offenbach</a>’s opera <em>Barkouf</em>, where a dog rules the day.</p>
<p>These musicians present this rare gem for the first time in the UK in a concert performance at The Bridgewater Hall in 2026.</p>
<p>Multi-award-winning actor, writer and comedian Alistair McGowan joins the cast as Narrator.</p>
<p>Join us for a tail-wagging triumph of opera at its most unexpected!</p>
<h3>Overview</h3>
<p>Step into the absurd political world of Offenbach’s <em>Barkouf</em> — a riotous opera where corruption runs wild, flattery is an art form and the only thing more dangerous than power are the incompetent politicians desperate to win it …</p>
<p>When a dog is made governor of the fictitious city of Lahore, laughter turns to applause as he rallies the people and proves that even the unlikeliest hero can change history. Filled with dazzling melodies, biting satire and boundless heart, <em>Barkouf</em> is a riotous romp through pomp, politics and power that is as relevant today as it was when it was first performed in 1860.</p>
<p>Opera in three acts.</p>

    <section class="main-content stack stack--l article--no-sidebar">
                    <div class="main-content__intro">
                <p>Two angels fall to earth. Heaven help them.</p>

            </div>
        
                    <div class="main-content__text  stack stack--l">
                <p><span data-contrast="auto">Angels appear all too rarely. Don’t miss them.</span><span data-ccp-props="{}"> </span></p>
<p><span data-contrast="auto">Care becomes contempt</span><span data-contrast="none">,</span><span data-contrast="none"> </span><span data-contrast="auto">and love becomes loathing in this dark, unsettling parable from contemporary composer </span><a href="https://www.eno.org/people/du-yun/"><span data-contrast="none">Du Yun</span></a><span data-contrast="auto"> and librettist </span><a href="https://www.eno.org/people/royce-vavrek/"><span data-contrast="none">Royce Vavrek</span></a><span data-contrast="auto">.</span><span data-ccp-props="{}"> </span></p>
<p><span data-contrast="auto">Breaking with operatic tradition, </span><a href="https://www.eno.org/operas/angels-bone/"><i><span data-contrast="none">Angel’s Bone</span></i></a><span data-contrast="auto"> fuses multiple musical genres, spoken word and immersive staging in an uncompromising tale of modern slavery and human trafficking.</span><span data-ccp-props="{}"> </span></p>
<p><span data-contrast="none">This UK premiere of the Pulitzer Prize-winning opera, an ENO production in collaboration with Factory International and the </span><a href="https://www.bbc.co.uk/philharmonic"><span data-contrast="none">BBC Philharmonic Orchestra</span></a><span data-contrast="none">, was staged at Aviva Studios, Manchester, in May and comes to London in October. The chorus is performed by </span><a href="https://www.kantoschamberchoir.com/"><span data-contrast="none">Kantos Chamber Choir</span></a><span data-contrast="none">, with the </span><a href="https://www.eno.org/about/orchestra/"><span data-contrast="none">Orchestra of ENO</span></a><span data-contrast="none"> joining for the London run.</span><span data-ccp-props="{}"> </span></p>
<p><span data-contrast="none">Don’t miss Du Yun’s </span><i><span data-contrast="none">Angel’s Bone</span></i><span data-contrast="none"> at the iconic London Coliseum this October – a bold, unsettling opera that will challenge and stay with you long after the curtain falls. Book tickets now.</span></p>
<h2>Overview</h2>
<p><span class="TextRun SCXW45868295 BCX0" lang="EN-GB" xml:lang="EN-GB" data-contrast="auto"><span class="NormalTextRun SCXW45868295 BCX0">Mr and Mrs </span></span><span class="TextRun SCXW45868295 BCX0" lang="EN-GB" xml:lang="EN-GB" data-contrast="none"><span class="NormalTextRun SCXW45868295 BCX0">X.E</span></span><span class="TextRun SCXW45868295 BCX0" lang="EN-GB" xml:lang="EN-GB" data-contrast="none"><span class="NormalTextRun SCXW45868295 BCX0"> </span></span><span class="TextRun SCXW45868295 BCX0" lang="EN-GB" xml:lang="EN-GB" data-contrast="auto"><span class="NormalTextRun SCXW45868295 BCX0">are a desperate couple facing </span><span class="NormalTextRun SCXW45868295 BCX0">financial crisis</span><span class="NormalTextRun SCXW45868295 BCX0"> and a crumbling marriage</span></span><span class="TextRun Highlight SCXW45868295 BCX0" lang="EN-GB" xml:lang="EN-GB" data-contrast="none"><span class="NormalTextRun SCXW45868295 BCX0">,</span></span><span class="TextRun SCXW45868295 BCX0" lang="EN-GB" xml:lang="EN-GB" data-contrast="auto"><span class="NormalTextRun SCXW45868295 BCX0"> and they long for a better life. When they discover the two bruised and battered angels in their garden, they bring them inside to nurse them back to life.</span></span><span class="EOP SCXW45868295 BCX0" data-ccp-props="{}"> </span></p>
<p><span data-contrast="auto">Care quickly turns to control. The couple seize the opportunity to exploit the spiritual beings in pursuit of fame and fortune.</span><span data-ccp-props="{}"> </span></p>
<p><span data-contrast="auto">Brutally clipping the angels’ wings to exploit this heavenly gift, the celestial beings are subjected to degrading, inhumane practices.</span><span data-ccp-props="{}"> </span></p>
<p><a href="https://www.eno.org/operas/angels-bone/"><span data-contrast="none">Discover the story of Angel’s Bone </span></a><span data-ccp-props="{}"> </span></p>
<h2>Staging & Score</h2>
<p><span data-contrast="auto">Royce Vavrek’s libretto explores the dark forces that drive people into the murky underworld of human trafficking. This is underpinned </span><span data-contrast="none">by</span><span data-contrast="auto"> Du Yun’s eclectic style, ranging from chamber music and cabaret to electronica </span><span data-contrast="none">and</span><span data-contrast="auto"> punk.</span><span data-ccp-props="{}"> </span></p>
<p><span data-contrast="auto">Director Kip Williams adds dynamic staging that immerses audiences in the production. By using projection and multiple viewing angles, Williams invites audiences to question their own part in the exploitation of the celestial beings.</span><span data-ccp-props="{}"> </span></p>
<h2>Singers & Creatives</h2>
<p><span data-contrast="auto">Kip Williams is making his ENO and UK opera debut with </span><i><span data-contrast="auto">Angel’s Bone.</span></i><span data-contrast="auto"> This production marks the continuation of his long-term creative collaboration with award-winning </span><span data-contrast="none">d</span><span data-contrast="auto">esigner Marg Horwell</span><span data-contrast="none">,</span><span data-contrast="none"> </span><span data-contrast="auto">whose recent successes include </span><i><span data-contrast="auto">The Maids</span></i><span data-contrast="auto"> at Donmar Warehouse, </span><i><span data-contrast="auto">The Picture of Dorian Grey </span></i><span data-contrast="auto">on Broadway and an upcoming production of </span><i><span data-contrast="auto">Dracula</span></i><span data-contrast="auto"> starring Cynthia Erivo in the West End.</span><span data-ccp-props="{}"> </span></p>
<p><span data-contrast="auto">Internationally renowned conductor Baldur Brönniman, who trained at Manchester’s Royal Northern College of Music and is deeply committed to making classical music relevant in the 21</span><span data-contrast="auto">st</span><span data-contrast="auto"> century, leads the performances.</span><span data-ccp-props="{}"> </span></p>
<p><span data-contrast="auto">In the role of </span><span data-contrast="none">the </span><span data-contrast="auto">couple are Scottish mezzo-soprano and singing actress Allison Cook and British baritone Rodney Earl Clarke. Cook makes a welcome return to ENO following her critically acclaimed performance as Judith in </span><a href="https://www.eno.org/discover-opera/articles/an-introduction-to-duke-bluebeards-castle/"><i><span data-contrast="none">Duke Bluebeard’s Castle</span></i></a><i><span data-contrast="auto"> in </span></i><span data-contrast="auto">2024. Clarke has extensive </span><span data-contrast="none">onstage experience</span><span data-contrast="auto">, with his musical repertoire spanning opera and musical theatre.</span><span data-ccp-props="{}"> </span></p>
<p><span data-contrast="auto">The role of Girl Angel is performed by Swedish cross-genre musician and voice actress Mariam Wallentin, making her ENO debut. Best known as one half of the acclaimed duo Wildbirds & Peacedrums, her work spans experimental opera, including </span><i><span data-contrast="auto">The Wasp Factory</span></i><span data-contrast="auto">. </span><span data-contrast="none">Scottish tenor Matthew McKinney joins her as the character Boy Angel, </span><span data-contrast="auto">and Hong Kong countertenor Keith Pun as Male Soprano.</span><span data-ccp-props="{}"> </span></p>
<p><span data-contrast="auto">This production has been made possible through the </span><a href="https://www.eno.org/support-us/"><span data-contrast="none">generous support of a syndicate</span></a><span data-contrast="auto"> comprising Professor Mick Peake OBE.</span><span data-ccp-props="{}"> </span></p>

            </div>

                <div class="accordion-item" data-accordion-item>

                        role="button"

                    >
                        <h3 class="accordion-item__heading">
                            What kind of opera is Angel’s Bone?
                        </h3>
                        <span class="accordion-item__icon btn btn--mask-icon btn--square" aria-hidden="true" ></span>
                    </button>

                                        <div class="accordion-item__content-panel" id="accordion-10-1" inert data-parent="#10" data-accordion-content>
                        <div class="accordion-item__content">

                            
                            <p><em><span class="TextRun SCXW197257466 BCX0" lang="EN-GB" xml:lang="EN-GB" data-contrast="none"><span class="NormalTextRun SCXW197257466 BCX0">Angel’s Bone</span></span></em><span class="TextRun SCXW197257466 BCX0" lang="EN-GB" xml:lang="EN-GB" data-contrast="none"><span class="NormalTextRun SCXW197257466 BCX0"> is a groundbreaking opera-theatre work that combines an eclectic musical style</span><span class="NormalTextRun SCXW197257466 BCX0">,</span><span class="NormalTextRun SCXW197257466 BCX0"> ranging from hauntingly beautiful melodies to edgy, experimental textures. This compelling production delves deeply into themes of human exploitation, </span><span class="NormalTextRun SCXW197257466 BCX0">resilience</span><span class="NormalTextRun SCXW197257466 BCX0"> </span><span class="NormalTextRun SCXW197257466 BCX0">and redemption, offering a raw and emotionally charged narrative.     <section class="main-content stack stack--l article--no-sidebar">
                    <div class="main-content__intro">
                <p>The art of resistance</p>

            </div>
        
                    <div class="main-content__text  stack stack--l">
                <p>Where love is dangerous, power is corrupt and art is under attack.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.eno.org/people/giacomo-puccini/">Puccini</a>’s classic thriller, <em>Tosca</em>, unfolds in a world of desire, fear and resistance, where nothing feels safe and every choice has consequences.</p>
<p>One of opera’s most electrifying works, <a href="https://www.eno.org/operas/tosca/"><em>Tosca</em></a> moves at breathless pace through desire, betrayal and sacrifice, powered by Giacomo Puccini’s soaring score and a heroine forced to confront the brutal limits of love and loyalty. In Annilese Miskimmon’s gripping new ENO production, <em>Tosca</em> becomes impossible to look away from.</p>
<p>Book your <em>Tosca</em> tickets now and experience the drama of this unforgettable opera live on the iconic London Coliseum stage in 2026.</p>
<h2>Overview</h2>
<p>Following the critical success of <a href="https://www.eno.org/operas/dead-man-walking/"><em>Dead Man Walking</em></a> in 2025, ENO’s Artistic Director <a href="https://www.eno.org/people/annilese-miskimmon/">Annilese Miskimmon</a> reimagines this timeless opera, exploring the art of resistance and love in the face of political censorship.</p>
<p>Set in a concert hall in an unidentified European state overtaken by civil conflict, opera singer Floria Tosca plans a secret meeting with her lover, the painter Mario Cavaradossi. When the corrupt police chief Scarpia intervenes, a place of music is transformed into a site of fear and violence. Over the course of one night, Tosca is forced to fight for her love, her honour and her life.</p>
<p>More than a love story. This is an opera about resistance in the face of oppression, and the enduring power of love and art to defy tyranny.</p>
<p>Enjoy <em>Tosca</em> as a stand-alone performance, or as a companion piece to Kaija Saariaho’s <a href="https://www.eno.org/events/adriana-mater/"><em>Adriana Mater</em></a> as part of a broader exploration of the human cost of war and the resilience of the human spirit. Both operas feature in our unmissable 2026/27 season.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.eno.org/support-us/current-supporters/">Principal Production Sponsors</a>: George & Patti White</p>
<p><a href="https://www.eno.org/operas/tosca/">Discover the story of <em>Tosca</em></a></p>
<h2>Staging and Score</h2>
<p>The mid-century inspired architecture of the concert hall setting forms a backdrop to this revolutionary new take on one of the world’s most performed operas.</p>
<p>Featuring some of <a href="https://www.eno.org/discover-opera/articles/puccinis-greatest-arias/">Puccini’s most famous arias</a>, including <em>Vissi d’arte (Love and Music)</em> and<em> E lucevan le stelle, d’arte (With the Stars Shining Brightly),</em> this iconic score seamlessly connects and contrasts the fast-paced plot with the tenderness of Tosca and Cavaradossi’s romance. Its quick-shifting tempos and intensity will leave hearts pounding and pulses racing in this must-see production, sung in an English translation by Amanda Holden.</p>
<h2>Singers and Creatives</h2>
<p>Making her ENO debut, internationally acclaimed Grammy Award winner Axelle Fanyo takes on the role of Tosca, with her lover Cavaradossi played by tenor Chaz’men Williams-Ali. Sadistic police chief Scarpia is brought to life by Christopher Purves and later in the run, Craig Colclough.</p>
<p>After his acclaimed performances of <a href="https://www.eno.org/operas/la-boheme/"><em>La bohème</em> </a>in 2022, where he “drew out a truly glorious performance from the ENO Orchestra” (Bachtrack), we welcome the return of internationally renowned conductor Ben Glassberg.</p>
<p>This production has been made possible through the <a href="https://www.eno.org/support-us/">generous support of a syndicate</a> comprising J.S. Murdoch, Kieran Cooper, Neville Astley & Isabel Radage and Leo Toralballa.</p>
<p>The Children’s Choir is generously supported by Melissa Disney.</p>

                <p>A daughter of sacrifice</p>

            </div>
        
                    <div class="main-content__text  stack stack--l">
                <p>A family divided by destiny, reunited by hope. <a href="https://www.eno.org/people/christoph-gluck/">Gluck</a>’s rarely performed opera,<em> Iphigénie en Tauride</em> makes its ENO debut in a new staging for 2026/27 by Olivier award-winning director Lyndsey Turner.</p>
<p>Book your tickets for<em> Iphigénie en Tauride</em> and experience an operatic masterpiece in this new production, live at the London Coliseum in 2026.</p>
<h3><strong>Overview</strong></h3>
<p>Iphigénie and her brother Oreste are the children of the most blood-soaked dynasty in Greek history. Their inheritance is a legacy of violence dating back to the dawn of time.</p>
<p>Her journey has taken her to a forlorn temple at the ends of the earth. His has taken him to the edge of madness. Each fears the other is dead.</p>
<p>Stranded on a remote island, forced to minister to the wishes of a terrifying ruler, Iphigenie dreams of home. The hope that she will one day reunite with her brother Oreste is all that stands between her and despair.</p>
<p>So, when a mysterious stranger washes up on the island’s shores with news of the collapse of her family, Iphigenie fears the worst. But is all as hopeless as first seems? Or is there more to this stranger than meets the eye?</p>
<p>Find out what fate has in store for the siblings, in a new interpretation of this rarely performed operatic masterpiece.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.eno.org/operas/iphigenie-en-tauride/">Discover the story of <em>Iphigénie en Tauride</em> </a></p>
<h3><strong>Staging and score</strong></h3>
<p>Widely regarded as Gluck’s most important work, <em>Iphigénie en Tauride </em>will be performed in its original French libretto by Nicolas-François Guillard with English surtitles projected above the stage.</p>
<h3><strong>Singers and creatives</strong></h3>
<p>Baroque specialist David Bates makes his ENO debut on the podium, while Lyndsey Turner directs.</p>
<p>Christine Rice leads the cast as Iphigénie after her unforgettable performance in <em><a href="https://www.eno.org/operas/dead-man-walking/">Dead Man Walking</a>, </em>with her brother Oreste played by Jacques Imbrailo.</p>
<p>This production has been made possible through the <a href="https://www.eno.org/support-us/">generous support of a syndicate</a> comprising Kathryn Uhde, Stephen & Margaret Bickford-Smith, Liz Cratchley OBE, Vincent Mercer & Mrs Anzo Francis, Frances Tait, Su-Mei & Marcus Thompson, Mark Tousey and Elizabeth Wright.</p>

    <section class="text-block section">
        <h4>Operas</h4>
<p>Each year, our brilliant artistic team curates an exciting Season from eternal classics to contemporary pieces pushing the opera to its limits.</p>
<p>This year is no different, productions old and new from opera’s greatest composers to new stars, we are excited to bring to you the whole range of the<a href="https://www.eno.org/about/this-season/"> operatic repertoire in one Season</a>.</p>

<section
  aria-label="Nights at the Bush, now for less"  class="full_content white_bg pt_lrg pb_lrg"
> <!-- Full Content -->

  <div class="mw_720 no_text_center"> <!-- MW -->

    <h2 class="h2">Nights at the Bush, now for less</h2>
    <p><strong>We’ve changed how our tickets are priced to make it simpler than ever. We’re making more £15 tickets available than ever before, and we’ve got rid of dynamic pricing so ticket prices won’t change.</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>Standard tickets range from £15 to £45 in the Holloway Theatre, and £15 to £25 in the Studio. <a href="https://www.bushtheatre.co.uk/fifteen-pound-tickets/">Find £15 tickets.</a></li>
<li>Concessions offer £5 off standard price tickets above £20. Available for students, senior citizens, disabled and unemployed / unwaged patrons.</li>
<li>Under 30s and Locals can get up to £10 off tickets and discounts at the bar with a <a href="https://www.bushtheatre.co.uk/visit/memberships/">free Bush membership.</a></li>
</ul>
<p>We never charge booking fees on any of our tickets whenever you book directly with us. We recommend only booking directly with us, or from one of our authorised agents. Our authorised agents include TodayTix and Official London Theatre.</p>

                  </div>
       <!-- / Button Repeater -->

  </div> <!-- / MW -->

</section> <!-- / Full Content -->




<section

    <h2 class="h2">Ticket FAQs</h2>
    
    
          <div class="accordion__list_block"> <!-- Accordion List Block -->
                <ul role="tablist">
          
          
          
            <li>
              <div class="accordion__btn"> <!-- FAQ Btn -->
                                <a href="#block_f1faea5a640e8a9869ef60ee9537be50-accordion-1" data-tab="block_f1faea5a640e8a9869ef60ee9537be50-accordion-1" role="tab" title="How do I book tickets?" aria-label="How do I book tickets?" aria-controls="block_f1faea5a640e8a9869ef60ee9537be50-accordion-1" aria-expanded="false" aria-haspopup="true">
                  <div class="accordion__icon"> </div>
                  <h3>How do I book tickets?</h3>                </a>
              </div> <!-- / FAQ Btn -->
              <div class="accordion__cont accordion__cont--no_image" id="block_f1faea5a640e8a9869ef60ee9537be50-accordion-1"> <!-- Accordion Cont -->

                <div class="accordion__text_col"> <!-- Accordion Text Col -->

                  <p><strong>Online:</strong> Tickets can be booked online quickly and securely 24 hours a day. <a href="https://www.bushtheatre.co.uk/whats-on/">Click here.</a></p>
<p><strong>By phone:</strong> Call our Box Office on 020 8743 5050. There is no booking fee. The Box Office line is open 4pm – 8pm Monday to Saturday.</p>
<p><strong>In person:</strong> Our Box Office is open 5pm-8pm Monday to Saturday. Please note, we are currently a cashless venue.</p>
<p> </p>

                <div class="accordion__text_col"> <!-- Accordion Text Col -->

                  <p>Standard tickets range from £15 to £45 in the Holloway Theatre, and £15 to £25 in the Studio. Concessions offer £5 off standard tickets.</p>
<p>Prices may vary between productions. Be sure to check out individual production pages for accurate pricing details.</p>
<p>Special event ticket prices may vary, check the individual events for more details.</p>

            <li>

                  <p>Access tickets, wheelchair spaces and free Personal Assistant / Companion tickets can be booked online, over the phone or in person.</p>

                  <div class="accordion__icon"> </div>
                  <h3>What discounts and concessions are available?</h3>                </a>
              </div> <!-- / FAQ Btn -->
              <div class="accordion__cont accordion__cont--no_image" id="block_f1faea5a640e8a9869ef60ee9537be50-accordion-4"> <!-- Accordion Cont -->

                <div class="accordion__text_col"> <!-- Accordion Text Col -->

                  <p>We offer discounted Concession rate tickets for students, senior citizens, disabled and unemployed / unwaged patrons. Free tickets are also available for Personal Assistants.</p>
<p>If you’re under 30 or live or work in a 2 mile radius of the Bush, you can <a href="https://www.bushtheatre.co.uk/visit/memberships/">sign up for free as a member</a> to access exclusive discounts on tickets and at the bar.</p>

                  <div class="accordion__icon"> </div>
                  <h3>How do I book a season ticket?</h3>                </a>
              </div> <!-- / FAQ Btn -->
              <div class="accordion__cont accordion__cont--no_image" id="block_f1faea5a640e8a9869ef60ee9537be50-accordion-5"> <!-- Accordion Cont -->

                <div class="accordion__text_col"> <!-- Accordion Text Col -->

                  <p>The more you book, the more you save. Add tickets for more than one production to your basket and the savings will be applied automatically.</p>

                   <!-- Button Repeater -->
                    <div class="accordion__buttons">
                      
                                                  <a class="btn green_btn" href="https://www.bushtheatre.co.uk/visit/ways-to-save/" target="_self">Ways to Save</a>

Are there any last minute tickets?" aria-label="If the performance I want is sold out, how can I get tickets? Are there any last minute tickets?" aria-controls="block_f1faea5a640e8a9869ef60ee9537be50-accordion-6" aria-expanded="false" aria-haspopup="true">
                  <div class="accordion__icon"> </div>
                  <h3>If the performance I want is sold out, how can I get tickets? Are there any last minute tickets?</h3>                </a>
              </div> <!-- / FAQ Btn -->
              <div class="accordion__cont accordion__cont--no_image" id="block_f1faea5a640e8a9869ef60ee9537be50-accordion-6"> <!-- Accordion Cont -->

                <div class="accordion__text_col"> <!-- Accordion Text Col -->

                  <p>If the performance you want is sold out, you may still be able to get tickets…</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Waiting List:</strong> we sometimes get tickets returned in advance. Email <a href="mailto:boxoffice@bushtheatre.co.uk">boxoffice@bushtheatre.co.uk</a> a contact number, 3 preferred dates and the number of tickets you would like. Please note we cap the waiting list at 10 people per performance.</li>
<li><strong>Returns Queue:</strong> we often get tickets returned just before the show. These tickets will be offered to a returns queue in person at the Box Office on a first-come, first-served basis. You can join the queue from 2 hours before the show.</li>
<li><strong>Join as a supporter:</strong> become a supporter from just £30 a month to unlock benefits including the best seats for every production, even after the show has sold out. <a href="https://www.bushtheatre.co.uk/support/star-supporters/">Click here to find out more and join now.</a></li>
</ul>

                                          </div>

" aria-label="How will I receive my tickets? " aria-controls="block_f1faea5a640e8a9869ef60ee9537be50-accordion-7" aria-expanded="false" aria-haspopup="true">
                  <div class="accordion__icon"> </div>
                  <h3>How will I receive my tickets? </h3>                </a>
              </div> <!-- / FAQ Btn -->
              <div class="accordion__cont accordion__cont--no_image" id="block_f1faea5a640e8a9869ef60ee9537be50-accordion-7"> <!-- Accordion Cont -->

                <div class="accordion__text_col"> <!-- Accordion Text Col -->

                  <p>We use contactless e-tickets on all orders. When you book, you will receive e-tickets sent to your email address. You can also access these by <a href="https://www.bushtheatre.co.uk/my-account/">logging in to your account</a> and clicking ‘E-tickets’.</p>
<p>We will also send you an SMS text message on the day of your performance, with a link to your mobile tickets.</p>
<p>You will need to show your tickets on your phone or mobile device when entering the auditorium, so make sure you have them ready. There is no need to print your e-tickets.</p>

                   <!-- / Button Repeater -->

                <div class="accordion__text_col"> <!-- Accordion Text Col -->

                  <p>In the <strong>Holloway Theatre</strong> (the Bush Theatre’s main house), seats are 53cm wide, with a gap of between 7cm and 14cm between each seat. Seats do not have arm rests.</p>
<p>In the <strong>Studio</strong>, seats are 45cm wide, with a gap of 7cm between each seat. Seats do not have arms rests.</p>

                <p class="h2">About</p>
                <div id="">
<p><span style="font-weight: 400">Bhopal. India. 1984.</span></p>
<p><b><i>I walk home. The skyline is changed.<br />
</i></b><b><i>The skeleton is fast becoming a huge metal creature.<br />
</i></b><b><i>They have built a behemoth here.</i></b></p>
<p><span style="font-weight: 400">Born under a blue sky in a city of lakes, a girl grows up with her father and sister. The three of them together, always.</span></p>
<p><span style="font-weight: 400">But as she grows, the land begins to change. A giant factory rises over her town. Her mother always wanted more for them – now the girl wants more too.</span></p>
<p><span style="font-weight: 400">Then comes the night that tears everything apart.</span></p>
<p><span style="font-weight: 400">Ferocious, brutal and damning, this epic story of a life ravaged by ecological disaster is written by </span><b>Titas Halder</b><span style="font-weight: 400"> (</span><i><span style="font-weight: 400">Foal</span></i><span style="font-weight: 400">, Finborough), directed by </span><b>Matthew Xia </b><span style="font-weight: 400">(</span><i><span style="font-weight: 400">Tambo & Bones</span></i><span style="font-weight: 400">, ATC / Stratford East) and stars <strong>Linnea Berthelsen </strong>(<em>Stranger Things</em>)<strong>.</strong></span></p>
</div>
<p>Following the run at the Bush, <em>Darkling</em> will be embarking on a UK tour. <a href="https://www.atctheatre.com/production/darkling-2026/">Find out more here.</a></p>

            </div>

              <a href="#team-listing-item-15165" class="team-listing__minimal-post team-listing__popup-link" > <!-- Minimal Post -->

                <div class="team-listing__minimal-flex" >
                                      <p>Writer</p>
