                      </div> <!-- / Image Container -->
                                        <p class="h3" >Titas Halder</p>
                                          <p class="h5" >Writer</p>
                                        <div class="divider" ></div>
                                          <p><strong>Titas Halder</strong> is a writer and director working across Theatre, Film and Music. He is currently Associate Artistic Director at the Donmar Warehouse. As a writer he trained on the Royal Court Theatre Young Writers’ Programme.</p>
<p>His first two plays <em>Run the Beast Down</em> and <em>Escape the Scaffold</em> saw him nominated for Best Writer at the inaugural Stage Debut Awards and acclaimed as a rising star playwright. The same year, his play The Basement was a finalist for the Verity Bargate Award.</p>
<p>His next play Replica premiered at the National Theatre as part of NT Connections, and was also produced at Riksteatern’s Länk Festival in Stockholm. His latest play<em> Foal</em> premiered at the Finborough Theatre in London in 2026. He was selected for BBC Voices 2024 and is currently writing his first feature film for Storyteller.</p>
                                        <div class="clear"></div>
                  </div> <!-- / Content -->
                </div> <!-- / Pop-up -->

            </li>
                      <li>
              <a href="#team-listing-item-15145" class="team-listing__minimal-post team-listing__popup-link" > <!-- Minimal Post -->
                <h4>Matthew Xia</h4>
                <div class="team-listing__minimal-flex" >
                                      <p>Director</p>
                                    <img decoding="async" src="https://www.bushtheatre.co.uk/wp-content/themes/bush_theatre/images/button_bg_arrow_dark.svg" alt="" />
                </div>
              </a> <!-- / Minimal Post -->

              <div class="team-listing__popup mfp-hide" id="team-listing-item-15145" > <!-- Pop-up -->
                  <button class="mfp-close" type="button" title="Close Pop-up" >
                    <span>X</span>
                  </button>
                  <div class="team-listing__popup-content " > <!-- Content -->
                                          <div class="team-listing__popup-image" > <!-- Image Container -->
                        <img decoding="async" src="https://www.bushtheatre.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/matthewxia-320x480.jpg" alt="" />
                      </div> <!-- / Image Container -->
                                        <p class="h3" >Matthew Xia</p>
                                          <p class="h5" >Director</p>
                                        <div class="divider" ></div>
                                          <p>Matthew Xia is a multiple award-winning theatre director, cultural leader, and multi-disciplinary artist whose work moves fluidly between stages, streets, and communities. Matthew began his career at Stratford East as a young actor and DJ under the name Excalibah; this unorthodox path through performance, music, and a love of audiences continues to inform his distinctive approach to making work.</p>
<p>Matthew Xia is the Artistic Director of ATC (Actors Touring Company). He was previously Associate Artistic Director at the Royal Exchange Theatre, Manchester, where he established OPEN EXCHANGE, an artist development scheme for more than 400 next generation theatre-makers; Director-in-Residence at Liverpool Everyman & Playhouse; and Associate Director at Theatre Royal Stratford East. He was also Associate Artist at Nottingham Playhouse alongside James Graham and Amanda Whittington.</p>
<p>Across his career, Matthew has directed some of the UK’s most talented actors, including Daniel Kaluuya, Cynthia Erivo, Joseph Quinn, Erin Doherty, Malachi Kirby, Maxine Peake, David Haig, Samuel Barnett, Matt Henry, Karl Collins, Martina Laird, Christopher Colquhoun, and David Moorst.</p>
<p>His directing credits include: <em>Tender</em> (Soho Theatre); <em>Small Island</em> (Leeds Playhouse / Birmingham REP / Nottingham Playhouse / ATC); <em>The Harder They Come</em> (Stratford East); <em>Bodies of Water</em> (ATC / GDIF); <em>Skeleton Crew</em> (Donmar Warehouse); <em>The Architect</em> (GDIF / ATC / Stephen Lawrence Day Foundation); <em>Tambo & Bones</em> (ATC / Theatre Royal Stratford East); the Olivier Award-winning <em>Hey Duggee – The Live Theatre Show</em> (Kenny Wax Family Entertainment / Cuffe & Taylor); the Fringe First Award-winning <em>Feeling Afraid as if Something Terrible is Going to Happen</em> (Francesca Moody Productions / Bush Theatre); <em>Rice</em> (ATC / Orange Tree); <em>The Wiz</em> (Ameena Hamid Productions / Hope Mill / BBC Big Night of Musicals); <em>Family Tree</em> (GDIF / ATC / Belgrade / Brixton House); <em>846Live</em> (Stratford East / GDIF); Amsterdam (ATC / Orange Tree / Theatre Royal Plymouth); Blood Knot (Orange Tree); <em>Eden</em> (Hampstead Theatre); <em>One Night In Miami…</em> (Nottingham Playhouse / Bristol Old Vic / HOME); <em>Into The Woods</em> and <em>Frankenstein</em> (Royal Exchange); <em>Wish List</em> (Royal Exchange / Royal Court); <em>Shebeen</em> (Nottingham Playhouse / Stratford East); <em>Sleeping Beauty and The Blacks</em> (Stratford East); <em>Dublin Carol</em> (Sherman Theatre); <em>Blue/Orange </em>and <em>The Sound of Yellow</em> (Young Vic); <em>Sizwe Banzi is Dead</em> (Young Vic / Eclipse); <em>I Was Looking at the Ceiling and Then I Saw the Sky</em> (co-director, Stratford East / Barbican); and <em>Suckerpunch Boom Suite</em> (Barbican / NitroBEAT).</p>
<p>As both director and dramaturg, Matthew has worked with an array of renowned writers including Suzan-Lori Parks, Dominique Morisseau, Arinze Kene, April De Angelis, Joe Penhall, Vikki Stone, Katherine Soper, David Levi-Addai, Yasmin Joseph, Mojisola Adebayo, and Nessah Muthy. He has also been a respected panelist for the Evening Standard Future Fund, the Yale Drama Series, the Alfred Fagon Award, BEAM, the Bruntwood Prize, and, most recently, the Eurovision Song Contest.</p>
<p>Beyond directing, Matthew’s practice spans music, sound, and live event culture. His work as a DJ, composer and sound designer includes presenting an award-winning hip-hop show on BBC 1Xtra; DJing for the London 2012 Paralympic Games Opening Ceremony; and creating work for productions including <em>The People Are Singing</em> (Royal Exchange), <em>Free Run</em> (Underbelly), <em>That’s The Way To Do It</em> (TimeWon’tWait), <em>Pass The Baton</em> and <em>Bolero Remixed</em> (New London Orchestra), and <em>Da Boyz</em>, <em>Family Man</em>, <em>The Snow Queen</em>, <em>Hansel & Gretel</em>, <em>Medea</em>, and <em>Squid</em> (Stratford East).</p>
<p>Matthew was a founding member of Act for Change. In 2019, he was awarded an Honorary Doctorate from the University of the Arts London in recognition of his work to make theatre more accessible and to champion minority groups as leaders, makers, and audiences within the industry.</p>

<p>Niraj’s television and film soundtracks have reached a worldwide audience. <p>By contrast, Niraj’s album work allows him to explore and bring to life his own narrative. Albums include the critically acclaimed ‘Along The Dusty Road’, ‘The Lost Souls’ and ‘Mud Doll’.</p>
<p>Other work includes the score for the official Olympic Torch event on London’s South Bank (SBC). Musical <em>Wah! Wah!                                           <p><span style="font-weight: 400"><strong>Actors Touring Company</strong> (ATC) is a portable portal to the world. Through their work, they connect global artistic voices to local communities across the UK and beyond.</span></p>
<p><span style="font-weight: 400">ATC is the UK’s leading theatre producer of international plays. They source, commission and produce work from around the world and from the global cultures that exist within the UK. They create dialogue between here and the rest of the world, amplifying voices that have often been overlooked in British theatre.</span></p>
<p><span style="font-weight: 400">They explore global systems experienced at a human level: who gets to speak, who is seen, and who is centred.                 <p class="h2">About</p>
                <div id="">
<p><em><strong>“I feel like a newborn out in the world for the first time. I feel… ravenous.”</strong></em></p>
<p>Tonight’s the night. She’s got a plan. And it involves her (secret) girlfriend, and the house they’re about to move into together.</p>
<p>And it doesn’t matter to her that her mum warns tonight is the first night of the ghost month. Because parents will say anything to keep you home.</p>
<p>Swiping an orange from the family altar and pocketing a coin she finds on her way over to the new place, she steps through the doorway – and unwittingly invites a hungry ghost into both of their lives. As the ghost starts to take over and she wrestles for control of her own body, her carefully constructed house of lies comes tumbling down around her.</p>
<p>A sexy horror rom-com exploring what takes root in the space between superstition and rationality. Starring Olivier Award nominee <strong>Mei Mac</strong>, <em>The Hungry Ghost</em> is the debut play from <strong>Mei Leng Yew</strong>, directed by New Earth Theatre Artistic Director <strong>Ailin Conant</strong>.</p>
<p><em>(Further casting to be announced)</em></p>

<p>In 2025, she was shortlisted for the Women’s Play for Playwriting for her play<em> Down Side Up</em>.                                           <p><strong>Ailin</strong> is the Artistic Director of New Earth. <p>As a freelancer, Ailin is Senior Associate Director on <em>My Neighbour Totoro</em> with the RSC and Improbable, and has previously worked for the The Royal Court, Bush Theatre, Theatre503, Kansas City Rep (USA), Ayyam Al-Masrah (Gaza), Clown Me In (Lebanon), and The Catalyst (Switzerland).</p>

        <script>
            document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', function () {
                const calendarEl = document.getElementById('calendar');
                const listEl = document.getElementById('calendar-list');

                const events = [
                                    ];

                const calendar = new FullCalendar.Calendar(calendarEl, {
                    initialView: 'dayGridMonth',
                    showNonCurrentDates: false,
                    datesSet: function(dateInfo) {
                        // When the main calendar changes month, update the list view's date
                        listCalendar.gotoDate(dateInfo.start);
                    },
                    headerToolbar: {
                        left: 'prev,next today',
                        center: 'title',
                        right: ''
                    },
                    events: events,
                    eventDidMount: function(info) {
                        if (info.view.type.startsWith('list') && info.event.extendedProps.time) {
                            const timeCell = info.el.querySelector('.fc-list-event-time');
                            if (timeCell) {
                                timeCell.textContent = info.event.extendedProps.time;
                            }
                        }
                    },
                    eventContent: function(arg) {
                        if (window.innerWidth < 768) return null;

                        const title = arg.event.title;
                        const time = arg.event.extendedProps.time || '';
                        const status = arg.event.extendedProps.status || '';
                        const statusClass = arg.event.extendedProps.statusClass || '';

                        const wrapper = document.createElement('div');
                        wrapper.innerHTML = `
                            <div class="fc-title">${title} - ${time}</div>
                            ${status ? `<span class="${statusClass}">${status}</span>` : ''}
                        `;
                        return { domNodes: [wrapper] };
                    },
                    dateClick: function(info) {
                        const target = listEl.querySelector(`.fc-list-day[data-date="${info.dateStr}"]`);
                        if (target) {
                            target.scrollIntoView({ behavior: 'smooth', block: 'start' });
                            target.classList.add('highlighted');
                            setTimeout(() => target.classList.remove('highlighted'), 2000);
                        }
                    }
                });

                const listCalendar = new FullCalendar.Calendar(listEl, {
                    initialView: 'listMonth',
                    headerToolbar: false,
                    events: events,
                    eventDidMount: function(info) {
                        if (info.view.type.startsWith('list') && info.event.extendedProps.time) {
                            const timeCell = info.el.querySelector('.fc-list-event-time');
                            if (timeCell) {
                                timeCell.textContent = info.event.extendedProps.time;
                            }
                        }
                    }
                });

                calendar.render();
                listCalendar.render();

                // Initially hide calendar view
                document.getElementById('list-view').style.display = 'none';

                // Switch view toggle
                document.querySelectorAll('.switch-btn').forEach(button => {
                    button.addEventListener('click', function () {
                        document.querySelectorAll('.switch-btn').forEach(btn => btn.classList.remove('active'));
                        this.classList.add('active');

                        const view = this.dataset.view;
                        if (view === 'calendar-view') {
                            document.getElementById('calendar-view').style.display = 'block';
                            document.getElementById('list-view').style.display = 'none';
                        } else {
                            document.getElementById('calendar-view').style.display = 'none';
                            document.getElementById('list-view').style.display = 'block';
                        }
                    });
                });
            });
        </script>

            <div class="event_about__desc">
                <p class="h2">About</p>
                <h3>Following sold-out runs at the Bush Theatre and in the West End, our electrifying production transfers to New York.</h3>
<p>Meet Dre and Des, they are young, gifted, Black. He stayed. She left. Years later they come crashing back into each other’s lives, carrying new secrets and old scars. Caught in the space between memory and reality, they struggle to navigate the shifting borders that threaten to rewrite their past and reshape their future.</p>
<p>This epic and universal love story is about the enduring power of memory and young love. Olivier-nominee <strong>Heather Agyepong</strong> (<em>The Power</em>) reprises her role as Des. <strong>Daniel Ezra</strong> (<em>All American, The Running Man</em>) takes on the role of Dre.</p>
<p>Written by Bush Emerging Writers’ Group alum <strong>Benedict Lombe</strong> (<em>Lava</em>), directed by <strong>Lynette Linton</strong> (<em>Not Your Superwoman</em>), <em>Shifters</em> “<strong>redefines the romcom</strong>” (Financial Times)</p>
<p>Previews begin 6 July, performances until 30 August 2026, at Cherry Lane Theatre, New York’s oldest Off-Broadway theatre.</p>

Booking tickets

  • MEMBERSHIPS
  • GIFT VOUCHERS
  • CONTENT GUIDANCE
  • TICKET RESALE
  • TERMS & CONDITIONS

TICKETS

Tickets can be booked on our website — you can find a list of all of our productions by visiting What’s On.

what’s onwhat’s on

CONCESSIONS AND ACCESS

Concessions are subject to availability.

£23.50–£26.50 tickets can be booked by Access Members across all in person performances, plus one carer/companion ticket per booking available at the same price.  

The Access rate is available on Premium tickets on Audio Described, British Sign Language (BSL) Interpreted, Captioned and Relaxed performances. The Access rate is not available on Premium tickets for other performances or on Charitable tickets. 

You can book your Senior Citizen ticket on our website by selecting the Senior Citizens ticket option for the relevant performances.

How the Other Half Loves

Senior Citizens can book tickets priced between £45.50 and £71.50 for £34.50 on off-peak matinees only.

Martin Guerre

Senior Citizens can book tickets priced between £45.50 and £71.50 for £34.50 on all performances.

A Christmas Carol

Senior Citizens can book tickets priced between £46.50 and £81.50 for £34.50 on off-peak matinees only.

You can book an Under 16s ticket on our website by selecting the Under 16s ticket option for the relevant performances. Under 16s must be accompanied by an adult.

How the Other Half Loves

Under 16s receive 50% off tickets priced between £34.50 and £71.50 for off-peak performances.

Martin Guerre

Under 16s receive 50% off tickets priced between £34.50 and £71.50 for off-peak performances.

A Christmas Carol

Under 16s receive 50% off tickets priced between £36.50 and £81.50 for off-peak performances.

Tickets are available for schools groups of 10+ for Mon–Wed evenings and Wed matinees.

Please note: 10% deposit* will be taken at point of booking.

Visit Tickets for Schools for more information about each production or call our designated schools and groups line on 0344 871 7628.

*Deposits are non-refundable.

How the Other Half Loves

Off-peak Mon–Wed performances. £15 per ticket for UK state schools and £20 per ticket for UK fee-paying schools.

Martin Guerre

Off-peak Mon–Wed performances and weekday matinees. £15 per ticket for UK state schools and £20 per ticket for UK fee-paying schools.

A Christmas Carol

Off-peak Mon–Wed evenings and Tue–Thu matinees. £15 per ticket for UK state schools and £20 per ticket for UK fee-paying schools.

How the Other Half Loves

Groups of 10+ people can book tickets usually priced between £45.50 and £71.50 for £34.50 on all performances while availability remains.

Martin Guerre

Groups of 10+ people: £10 off tickets priced between £45.50 and £71.50 for off-peak performances.
Groups of 20+ people: £15 off tickets priced between £45.50 and £71.50 for off-peak performances.

A Christmas Carol

Groups of 10+ people: £5 off tickets priced between £46.50 and £81.50 for off-peak performances.

Book your tickets in person or over the phone by calling our designated schools and groups line on 0344 871 7628.

Please note: a 10% deposit* will be taken at point of booking.

Deposits are non-refundable.

MEMBERSHIPS

Access Membership

Become an Access Member to book your tickets online and pick the best seats in the house to suit your requirements. Our seat recommendations include step–free and wheelchair spaces and seats in the best positioning for captions, audio description and British Sign Language interpretation. 

Access membershipAccess membership

OV Local

Live in Lambeth or Southwark? Make the most of your visit with our free OV Local Membership.

OV localOV local

Supporter Memberships

Join as an OV TOGETHER Member and enjoy priority booking, special evenings and more.

join ov togetherjoin ov together

GIFT VOUCHERS

Buy a gift voucher and give the gift of an unforgettable theatre experience.

BUY GIFT VOUCHERSBUY GIFT VOUCHERS

CONTENT GUIDANCE

Find information on age and content guidance for our in person and streamed productions.

READREAD

TICKET RESALE

Tickets cannot be sold on or for commercial gain by any outlet other than The Old Vic or one of its authorised agents. We will void any ticket offered for resale at an inflated price, either on or offline, and urge audiences against buying tickets through these channels.

TERMS & CONDITIONS

Find information on the below topics and more:

  • E-Tickets
  • Booking fees
  • Terms and conditions
  • Returns and exchanges

But we can’t do it without your support.

Events at The Old Vic

A UNIQUE SPACE IN THE HEART OF WATERLOO

We offer a variety of packages, bespoke catering options, and attentive guidance to tailor your event to suit any occasion.

The events space, located on the top floor of the Backstage building, is flooded with natural light and has striking views across the London skyline with a terrace that can be dressed for any occasion.

Arranged over two levels, Backstage Cafe & Bar is a vibrant and versatile space. The mezzanine Script Library floor provides a creative setting, with a projecting balcony overlooking Waterloo Millennium Green.

FROM YOUR FIRST ENQUIRY TO THE FINAL SCENE

Whatever event you are hosting, the space offers a unique backdrop to make it unforgettable. It is the perfect location for: 

  • Breakfast meetings
  • Product & book launches
  • Corporate receptions
  • Panel talks
  • Press events
  • Private dinners
  • Festive events
  • Summer parties
  • Wedding & partnership receptions
  • Filming & photo shoots
  • Creative workshops
  • Auditions & readings.

Our experienced events team will support you every step of the way — from your first enquiry to the final scene.

By choosing to host your event with us, you will be supporting The Old Vic’s world‑class work on and off stage, helping to sustain our historic theatre and further our mission to ensure that anyone can experience, make and benefit from theatre.

School Visits to The Old Vic

We look forward to welcoming you and your school to The Old Vic. Below is some helpful information to make sure your visit runs as smoothly as possible.

On arrival please have your e-tickets ready to scan. We recommend that you arrive 30 minutes before the start time of the show you are watching.

The visiting school is responsible for their students at all times. When in or around the immediate vicinity of The Old Vic, students must be under the supervision of a school-appointed adult. The school-appointed adult must be an employee of the school.

Please consider where teachers are placed when watching the show in order to best support your students. For Old Vic projects we will provide one teacher ticket for every 10 students.

It is the school’s responsibility to ensure their students conduct themselves in an appropriate manner that is respectful of the building, staff and other audience.

The school-appointed adult will be responsible for the students for the duration of the visit including before, after or during the performance should any individuals choose to venture off the premises.

In Penny, our bar and cafe on the basement level, there are two loo blocks: a loo block of 11 cubicles and one accessible ‘roomier’ loo; and a separate loo block of seven urinals with two cubicles, one of which is an accessible ‘roomier’ loo.

There is also a separate wheelchair accessible loo and a separate gender neutral loo with an enclosed sink.

On the Baylis Circle level on the third floor there are two loo blocks: a loo block of 12 cubicles and one accessible ‘roomier’ loo; and a separate loo block of eight urinals, with one cubicle.

There is another wheelchair accessible loo within the auditorium itself available for those seeing a show.

The school must ensure that all phones are switched off or to airplane mode (rather than switching it to silent) to make sure everyone’s experience is as enjoyable as possible. Photos and filming are not allowed in the auditorium.

If you would like a box to store mobile phones in during the performance please speak to a member of the Front of House team on the day.

Please note that Penny, our all-day cafe and bar, is open to the public from 8am. Anyone under 18 will not be served at the bar and we ask the school-appointed adult to ensure no attempts to purchase alcohol are made.

Visiting groups are not permitted to consume their own food in the front of house spaces without prior arrangement.

Please refrain from eating during the show.

The school is responsible for the health and safety and safeguarding of the school group and schools will be expected to have appropriate and adequate insurance arrangements for their students.

Schools should prepare their own risk assessments. The Old Vic carries a public liability insurance, a copy of which is available on request.

Our Front of House team are on hand throughout the performance should you need any further information. To obtain a copy of our safeguarding policy, or if you would like to contact The Old Vic Designated Safeguarding Lead, please email safeguarding@oldvictheatre.com.
